Someone just tried to attack Pila8.com . We stopped them. In the past day, we had tons of scraping traffics targeting different parts of our infrastructure (database, storage blobs, identity service, etc.). At the same time, millions of legitimate requests continued normally. We cannot prove whether the objective was scraping, data access, or preparing an automated submission attack. But this is exactly why platform integrity matters (my cofounder Yi Zhong used to run integrity for Meta). The greatest threat to a voice AI dataset is not always someone stealing it. It is someone polluting it 🚮 Bots, account farms, duplicate submissions, cloned voices, manipulated recordings, and recycled AI-generated audio can quietly contaminate a training set. The dataset may look bigger while making your model worse, reinforcing synthetic artifacts, or producing no meaningful improvement at all. If a data provider cannot establish that its contributors are real, its voices are authentic, and its submissions pass serious integrity and quality controls, you may not be buying training data --> You may be buying contamination 🤡. We built Pila8 differently: - Real people contributing real voices - Strong integrity controls around access and submission - Multiple quality gates before data reaches customers - Systems designed to detect suspicious and synthetic behavior - Legitimate contributors earning money for work that improves real models - Infrastructure that keeps operating when automated abuse appears We will not disclose how those protections work. We will disclose the outcome: The invalid traffic was rejected. Protected data remained protected. Legitimate contributors kept working 🚀 For teams building speech recognition, voice AI, multilingual models, or audio intelligence, data quality is not just about sample rate, labels, and dataset size. It starts with knowing there is a real human behind the voice. Need high-quality voice data you can actually trust? Let’s talk. #VoiceAI #AudioAI #SpeechAI #AIResearch #TrainingData #DataIntegrity #MachineLearning ...more ...more

“Hey Siri, read me my horoscope.” “Got it, releasing your source code.” Ok, maybe your daily horoscope app isn't connected to your repo, but the truth is voice interfaces are no longer just producing transcripts for humans to skim. They’re feeding tool calls, database writes, routing logic, form fills, code editors, CRMs, EHRs, and code agents. In that world, one corrupted structured token can break the whole workflow. That is why we built VoiceCodeBench 2.0: a benchmark for the ASR failure mode that matters most in real voice workflows... structured-token recovery. For decades, Word Error Rate has been the default way to measure ASR quality. But WER treats a dropped “the” the same as a corrupted account number, a mangled file path, a broken URL, or a wrong dosage. When speech-to-text becomes software input, that distinction is everything. VoiceCodeBench asks a different question: Does your ASR preserve the exact entities that downstream systems need to parse, store, compare, or execute? Across 12 ASR systems, we found: - The best system by WER, at 8.6%, still failed to recover all structured values in 31.3% of recordings - URLs, commands, file paths, and email addresses accounted for 59.6% of all entity failures - WER was informative, but not deterministic, for actual value recovery The benchmark includes: - 300 human-recorded workplace segments - 85 speakers - 1,482 audited entities - 26 entity types - 8 workflow domains, from IT/dev to healthcare and finance - Two new metrics: CTEM for entity-level recovery and TSR for full-workflow success We tested Deepgram, OpenAI, Google Cloud, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, Amazon Transcribe, and Whisper in both batch and streaming modes. Top-line results: - Deepgram Nova-3 had the best WER, 8.6%, and best TSR, 68.7% - ElevenLabs Scribe v2 had the best CTEM, 91.6% - Streaming consistently degraded structured-token recovery compared with batch - The gap between “readable transcript” and “usable for automation” is real and measurable For anyone building voice agents: WER is not enough. You need to know which entity types break, how often full workflows fail, and where to add confirmation prompts, validation, or human review. VoiceCodeBench 2.0 is fully open under MIT. Dataset: https://lnkd.in/g9JYAhZU White paper: https://lnkd.in/g7iX7KP3 If your speech-to-text system feeds automation, you should know your CTEM and TSR — not just your WER. #ASR #SpeechRecognition #VoiceAI #VoiceAgents #Benchmark #MachineLearning #AI #OpenSource #BesimpleAI ...more ...more

Your voice AI loses ready-to-pay customers 1 out of 10 times 🙈 You bought a voice AI agent. The one that promised to take calls 24/7, qualify leads, book appointments, and never miss a customer. But they silently dropped critical informations and produce plausible-looking but wrong output. Most vendors will tell you they have great word error rate (WER). And they probably do (like 2%). They’re using Deepgram, AssemblyAI, OpenAI. Even a simple wrapper looks impressive on WER. But WER is the wrong metric. WER treats every word: getting "the" wrong punishes the same as getting an address wrong. However, downstream LLM can recover from bad grammar, but it will dispatch your team to the wrong customer address. There had not been a way to test it reliably. So I am really proud of our team at Besimple AI 🍊 -- Tyler B. and Brandon T. -- who just open sourced this real human dataset which will demonstrate even the best model can get those things wrong 1 of out 10 times: https://lnkd.in/eyuTqipM . ...more ...more

🥦 Everyone Should Eat More Broccoli For over a month Besimple AI has been running on Broccoli 🥦 — our end-to-end feature agent — and it’s one of those moments where you realize the floor under the software industry is moving. You assign Broccoli a Linear ticket. It: • implements the feature end-to-end • reviews its own code • ships to production • debugs and fixes issues when something breaks in prod Broccoli 🥦 takes work that used to bounce between PM, engineer, reviewer, and oncall — and just… does it. Attached is our 🍊 Besimple AI's productivity chart since dogfooding Broccoli in December. We have shipped roughly 10x faster. Our engineers spend far less time buried in if-else statements and far more time designing systems, orchestrating agents, and solving harder problems. It’s the kind of environment where engineers level up fast — taking on larger scope, becoming stronger builders, and often the kind of people who go on to start companies themselves a few years later. We’re actively hiring founding engineers and summer interns. If you want to build where the future of software is happening (or know someone who does), shoot me a message. ...more ...more

The new Space website is live. I designed and built the site in 8 hours. Mostly consisted of a lot of back and forth on the motion and tiny details. The process was basically describing what I wanted, explaining what looked off, checking the output, and repeat. We wanted the site to show what Space feels like. That meant rebuilding Finder in React and making the product demos part of the page itself. Everything was designed and built in code - every scroll interaction, animation, and easter egg. As someone who made websites for many years by hand, it’s mind-blowing to see what can be achieved in such a short amount of time with the tools available today. Dekai Li and I are excited to officially announce Trident is part of Y Combinator’s Summer 2026 batch, and that we’ve raised our pre-seed from Y Combinator, with participation from Cory Levy (Z Fellows). Here’s why we built it: AI is accelerating how software is built, but on the opposite end, they’re also accelerating how attackers find and exploit vulnerabilities. As AI gets more powerful, that gap will only grow. We built Trident to defend companies at the same speed. What it does: 1. Scans every pull request for known n day, vulnerable dependencies, and logic flaws before merge 2. Safely runs scheduled, continuous penetration tests against your web apps, APIs, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes) We've found $10,000+ critical vulnerabilities across bug bounty programs and in half a dozen unicorns and prevented tens of millions in potential losses with our existing clients if youre curious to see what we can find feel free to send me a dm!

You may have Granola recording every Zoom meeting, but what about in office impromptu sessions? We built Berry so we don't lose our in-office conversations. And our office dog Juju made to Berry's transcript! This is what Berry means by "Juju interrupted work by sitting nearby." What is Berry? Berry is an internal tool we built. It is always on and records conversations in our office. Berry transcribes the conversations and then summarizes all decisions, to-dos, contexts, and chitchats. Recordings are deleted every night, and everyone at Besimple AI can query these summaries so we don't forget critical decisions discussed. Berry summaries are also used in other workflows, such as cross-checking with Linear tickets and Github commits, so decisions can be consistent across conversations, design docs, and code. Producing high quality human data remains very ops heavy, and that's why we invest in all these AI native workflows to reduce human errors in managing human operations.
